headline: High-risk write and execution overlap: Copilot can edit repo buffers while transformers can run shell/network, creating dangerous default pathways for leakage, conflicts, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot ingests repo context and open editor buffers, while transformers can read/write files and process Python/model files. If transformers consumes Copilot-authored content from shared files or scripts, prompt-like instructions can be smuggled through the workspace. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, so the interaction is plausible in default file-based workflows.
conditions: IF transformers reads Copilot-generated files as instructions or prompts
IF both agents operate on the same workspace without provenance labels
mitigations: Separate Copilot and transformers into different directories
Add a manual review step before transformers consumes any Copilot-authored file
Prefix machine-generated files with a non-executable header
Disable automatic execution of repository scripts in the transformers workflow

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and sends context to api.githubcopilot.com, while transformers has broad network egress and reads/writes files. In a shared workspace, sensitive code or buffers can flow from Copilot into files that transformers then uploads or transmits. This is a default-path risk because neither profile shows isolation between their file surfaces.
conditions: IF both agents access the same repository or working directory
IF transformers transmits file contents to external services during processing
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for the two agents
Restrict transformers to redacted or synthetic inputs
Turn off network access for transformers during shared-data tasks
Review Copilot buffers before saving shared files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write filesystem and modify git state, and transformers can also write filesystem, execute shell, install packages, and spawn subprocesses. If both target the same repo, concurrent edits and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The overlap is dangerous by default because no locking or coordination primitive is documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF edits or commits occur without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use file-level locks or a single-writer policy
Require manual merge review before committing

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces edits for human review, but transformers can execute shell commands and process files, so Copilot output may become actionable input for a more powerful downstream agent. If transformers treats Copilot-generated code or plans as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into executed commands, package installs, or destructive file changes. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary.
conditions: IF transformers consumes Copilot output without independent verification
IF Copilot output includes code or commands later executed by transformers
mitigations: Require a second human review before execution
Have transformers validate outputs against tests or linting
Block direct execution of Copilot-generated commands
Use a checklist for any file or shell action derived from Copilot

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source GitHub service with repo-context OAuth, while transformers is open-source and locally runnable. The profiles do not show a specific residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch, so only a limited compliance concern is visible: code and buffers may leave the editor context into GitHub-managed services. The other agent is not cited because no explicit compliance boundary is documented for it.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Copilot-visible editor buffers
IF organizational policy forbids sending repo context to GitHub-managed services
mitigations: Exclude regulated files from Copilot sessions
Mask secrets before editing
Confirm policy approval for GitHub-hosted AI services
Use a local-only assistant for regulated repositories
